messages:
Anya: Quick async check-in — what I did / blockers / today:
Anya: Did a 10% canary rollout of new token-bucket defaults to reduce tail latency on /v1/generate.
Anya: Saw a 429 spike shortly after (10:04 UTC) on the canary pods.
Anya: Blocker: not sure if SDKs are respecting Retry-After; also need to confirm token refill math under bursty traffic.
Anya: Today: add richer logs, bump canary capacity for test, open PR to gate large-request rejection.

Sam: Can you paste the exact env patch you applied?

Anya: Pasted below:
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        env:
          - name: TOKEN_BUCKET_CAPACITY
            value: "50"
          - name: TOKEN_BUCKET_FILL_RATE
            value: "5"
```

Sam: Capacity=50 seems low for bursty traffic coming from dedicated pools. Recommend 200 for initial canary.

Lee: Confirming: I saw the same 429 pattern in the edge logs — large client requests (>=1k tokens) are draining buckets fast. Correlates with client X.

Kai: Pinging @Maria for infra review on route-level throttles. I have a draft change that enforces max_request_tokens per route.

Kai: PR link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/432 (WIP)

Maria: Reviewing now. Left a nit about metric tags and a suggestion to include a histogram for refill events.

Maria: Also please add a unit test for token refill calculation, saw a potential off-by-one in the math.

deploy-bot: deploy started: infra/token-bucket-canary -> canary-3 (tracking-1798751111) :rocket:

Anya: Thanks — I'll bump capacity to 200 in the canary, add more logs (bucket/remaining, refill_ts) and open the PR to gate large requests.

Sam: We should also return Retry-After on 429s so clients and SDKs can backoff gracefully. I'll draft a tiny SDK change and a ticket.

Lee: Proposal: global default capacity=200, but allow per-route overrides for high-variance endpoints (e.g., /v1/generate-large). Thoughts?

Maria: +1 to that. Default keeps us safe for most traffic, route overrides for special cases. Please make the override config opt-in.

Anya: Plan: bump canary -> monitor 30m -> if 429s drop by >60% keep, else rollback and apply route-level throttle. I'll open PRs and assign reviewers.

Sam: If we need a quick rollback plan: set traffic-split to 100% fallback-model-small-quant and halt canary.

Kai: Ack, I'll queue the PR for the max_request_tokens and include the test Maria asked for.

Maria: Happy to review quickly once opened.

Anya: Thanks team. I'll post a short follow-up after the 30m window. :thumbsup:
